description.narrative: Contract related to: Contribution Agreement to Swedish International Development Cooperation (SIDA) for ACC "Climate Change Adaptation through watershed, forest and disaster risk management and governance." - The Action is structured around two objectives:1.  Improved and inclusive conservation, restoration and sustainable management and use of forests and biodiversity, within and outside protected areas ¿ including prevention of forest fires and implementation of climate adaptation and mitigation efforts; 2.  Strengthened environmental governance, access to justice, and rights protection for men and women, and indigenous peoples, according to their differentiated needs and roles.The first objective coincides with that of ACT-60734, aiming at reducing deforestation, forest degradation (mostly due to forest fires) and biodiversity loss. In this case, the objectove is reached through actions in support to civil society organisations working with local government and rural communities in and around forested areas. Field-level activities are expected to focus on the biomes of Amazon, Chiquitania and Chaco (CSO grants through the Swedish International Development Agency), which are the most vulnerable to land use change, fires and environmental degradation. Disaster risk reduction ¿ related to forest fires ¿ will be targeted with actions at community levels. Sustainable production practices and green value chains are expected to be supported, based on the recommendations of the EU-Bolivia Joint Review of the forest sector and potential alliance between public and private sector.The second objective will focus on more sensitive aspects of environmental and water management, dealing with governance, justice and environmental-territorial rights, with a special attention to indigenous people. As such, the intervention belongs to both priority areas 1 and 2, making their linkages visible. In partnership with the Swedish International Development Agency and through CSO, the intervention is expected to support access to environmental information and justice in accordance with the Bolivian commitment under the Escazú Agreement, promote and protect human right defenders working on land and environmental rights, foster community participation in local planning and their right to Free Prior and Informed Consent.

description.narrative: The United Nations defines sustainable land management (SLM) as the use of land resources, including soils, water, animals and plants, for the production of goods to meet changing human needs, while simultaneously ensuring the longterm productive potential of these resources and the maintenance of their environmental functions. This indicator measures how many people have been trained in sustainable land and water management practices.If monitoring capacity is limited or the context is fragile, this indicator could be simplified to monitor only the number of persons trained (without referring to an increase in knowledge and/or skills). However, in order to ensure the quality of training and the achievement of the desired result, it is recommended to assess the knowledge of participants before and after the intervention whenever possible.

description.narrative: The United Nations defines sustainable land management (SLM) as the use of land resources, including soils, water, animals and plants, for the production of goods to meet changing human needs, while simultaneously ensuring the longterm productive potential of these resources and the maintenance of their environmental functions. This indicator measures how many people have been trained in sustainable land and water management practices.If monitoring capacity is limited or the context is fragile, this indicator could be simplified to monitor only the number of persons trained (without referring to an increase in knowledge and/or skills). However, in order to ensure the quality of training and the achievement of the desired result, it is recommended to assess the knowledge of participants before and after the intervention whenever possible.

description.narrative: The ultimate objective of the Climate Change Convention (UNFCCC) is to achieve the stabilization of greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere at a level that would prevent dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system. Estimating the levels of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and removals is an important element of the efforts to achieve this objective. In accordance with Articles 4 and 12 of the Climate Change Convention and the relevant decisions of the Conference of the Parties, countries that are Parties to the Convention submit national GHG inventories to the Climate Change secretariat. These submissions are made in accordance with the reporting requirements adopted under the Convention, such as the revised Guidelines for the preparation of national communications by Parties included in Annex I to the Convention, Part I: UNFCCC reporting guidelines on annual greenhouse gas inventories (decision 24/CP.19) for Annex I Parties and Guidelines for the preparation of national communications for nonAnnex I Parties (decision 17/CP.8). The inventory data are provided in the annual GHG inventory submissions by Annex I Parties and in the national communications and biennial update reports by nonAnnex I Parties. The Paris Agreement adopted in 2015 marks the latest step in the evolution of the UN climate change regime and builds on the work undertaken under the Convention. Its central aim is to strengthen the global response to the threat of climate change by keeping a global temperature rise this century well below 2 degrees Celsius above preindustrial levels and to pursue efforts to limit the temperature increase even further to 1.5 degrees Celsius. The Agreement also aims to strengthen the ability of countries to deal with the impacts of climate change.Data reported against SDG indicators can be retrieved from the official UN SDG Database and Statistics https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/unsdg. One of the targets is: Substantially increase the number of countries with national and local disaster risk reduction strategies by 2020. In line with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 20152030, disaster risk reduction strategies and policies should mainstream and integrate disaster risk reduction within and across all sectors, across different timescales and with targets, indicators and time frames. These strategies should be aimed at preventing the creation of disaster risk, the reduction of existing risk and the strengthening of economic, social, health and environmental resilience.Data reported against SDG indicators can be retrieved from the official UN SDG Database and Statistics https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/unsdg.
